clue.text: Unbeatable batsman's 101-200, plus a single

parts.note: a batsman's runs from 101 to 200 make up a second century, or second ton, in cricket
a single is one

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator praises a batsman's big innings, scored right up to one run more.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a ton is a century of runs, so runs 101 to 200 are the batsman's second ton.
explanation.definitionFit: Something second to none has no superior, so it cannot be beaten.

clue.text: Footwear of the inexperienced ice skater?

definitions.text: Footwear of the inexperienced ice skater?

parts.words: Footwear of the inexperienced ice skater?
parts.note: a novice on the ice keeps losing their footing, so they are one who slips; the word is also a soft indoor shoe

explanation.surface: A question about what shoes a beginner skater should wear.
explanation.definitionFit: A slipper is a soft shoe for indoors, and also, whimsically, anyone who slips over.

clue.text: See 19 across
Despite an upset, they're minor changes in the main

definitions.text: they're minor changes in the main

indicators.note: an upset overturns things, so the letters of the two words beside it are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A sailor notes that, for all the turmoil, these are only small shifts at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is the poetic word for the sea; neap tides are those with the smallest range between high and low water.
explanation.definitionFit: Neap tides show the least rise and fall of the sea, so they are small changes in the ocean.

clue.text: More alcohol given to baby

parts.note: a pup is a baby animal, such as a young dog or seal

explanation.surface: Someone worries that drink has been given to an infant.
explanation.definitionFit: A top-up is a further pour to refill a glass, so it means more drink.

clue.text: Time boy surfacing above bottomless stream, breathing through this

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above the second
in a down clue, surfacing means coming upwards, so the letters are read from the bottom up

parts.note: a son is a boy

indicators.note: the stream word loses its final letter, its bottom in a down entry

parts.note: a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: A boy comes up for air after swimming in a deep stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surfacing' turns T and SON to give NOST; 'bottomless' cuts the last L from RILL to leave RIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostril is one of the nose openings that air passes through when you breathe.

clue.text: Order in row stinks

definitions.note: the clue's verb stands for the adjective meaning smelly, read as 'is what stinks'

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a row is a loud noise
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A complaint that the ranking in a row of seats is rotten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a command or arrangement, but here it is a British honour, the Order of Merit; 'stinks' stands for the adjective, as in 'what stinks'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something noisome has an offensive smell, so it is the kind of thing that stinks.

clue.text: Gather in grains, then reach under spruce

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece is placed below the first
the gathering word is placed inside the grains word

parts.note: sand is made of fine grains
to pick is to gather fruit or flowers
a span is a reach or extent

explanation.surface: A farmer harvests cereal and then stretches beneath a fir tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spruce' looks like the tree, but here it is the adjective meaning neat and smart.
explanation.definitionFit: Spick and span means very neat and clean, the same as spruce or smart.

clue.text: Flower border occupies me, with minor adjustment?

indicators.note: the border word moves into and fills the middle of the other piece
a small adjustment shifts the order of the letters slightly

parts.note: the setter of this puzzle signs as Paul, so 'me' is that name
a rim is a border or edge

explanation.surface: A gardener says a flowering plant fills the edge of his bed, give or take.
explanation.walkthrough: 'me' is the setter, Paul; 'with minor adjustment' swaps two letters to give PULA, which RIM occupies.
explanation.definitionFit: A primula is a flowering plant of the primrose family.

clue.text: One hand down skirts for warm feeling

indicators.note: to skirt something is to go around it, so the handing-down word surrounds the other

parts.note: to hand something down is to pass it on
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone passes down a skirt to another and feels fondness doing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Passion is strong emotion or ardour, a warm and intense feeling.

clue.text: Simple work cursory, for example?

definitions.meaning: Simple Simon is a children's verse, so a simple work for little ones
the word cursory is an example of a rhyme for nursery

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses a piece as plain and hasty.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursery rhyme is a simple traditional verse for children, such as Simple Simon.

clue.text: Unoriginal type wants to make Tom tom-tom?

definitions.meaning: someone who imitates others rather than thinking of their own ideas
a tom is a male cat, so making two of it means to copy the cat

explanation.surface: An unimaginative musician wants to turn a man named Tom into a drum.
explanation.definitionFit: A copycat is a person who imitates others, so an unoriginal sort.

clue.text: See 18
Prospect for this artist, left ear examination!

parts.note: prospectors pan for gold, whose chemical symbol is Au
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: An artist's prospects are hurt when a doctor checks his left ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prospect' looks like a view or outlook; here it is the verb, and gold (Au) is what is prospected for.
explanation.definitionFit: An aural is a listening test in a music exam, so a test of the ear.

clue.text: Revealing nothing, Labour leader elected assembly

indicators.note: an assembly puts the parts together in a new arrangement

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so only the first letter of Labour is used

explanation.surface: A Labour leader, revealing nothing, is voted in by the assembly.
explanation.walkthrough: O, L and ELECTED are rearranged by 'assembly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A décolleté neckline is cut low, so it is revealing.

clue.text: Criticise Chianti primarily, the scandal of Italian wine?

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so only the opening letter of the next word counts

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine
-gate is a suffix for a scandal, after Watergate

explanation.surface: A wine critic condemns a Chianti amid a scandal over Italian wine.
explanation.walkthrough: '-gate' attached to a word names a scandal, as in Watergate; so Asti-gate is the scandal of Italian wine.
explanation.definitionFit: To castigate is to rebuke or criticise severely.

clue.text: Forceful types reject any director's first films

indicators.note: only the first letter of director's is taken
to reject is to throw back, so the word any is read backwards

parts.note: a film of moisture is a mist

explanation.surface: Dynamic people refuse the first movies of any director.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reject' turns ANY to YNA; 'films' looks like movies but means mists.
explanation.definitionFit: Dynamists are people who believe in or display dynamism, forceful energetic types.

clue.text: One done up like a kipper?

definitions.text: One done up like a kipper?

parts.words: One done up like a kipper?
parts.note: a kipper is also a wide, garish tie of the 1970s, which is knotted, or done up, around the neck

explanation.surface: A question about a fish being dressed, smoked or prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: A kipper is a smoked herring, but a kipper tie is a very wide tie.
explanation.definitionFit: A necktie is fastened around the neck, and a kipper is one wide style of it.

clue.text: The whole time, standard in golf gets to threaten manipulative establishment?

parts.note: the mass of something is the bulk or whole of it
an age is a period of time
par is the standard number of strokes for a golf hole
to lour is to look threatening, like a dark sky

explanation.surface: A golfer always playing to standard threatens a shady business.
explanation.definitionFit: A massage parlour is a business where bodies are manipulated, often a euphemism.

clue.text: Advisory body meeting in smallest chamber?

definitions.meaning: a formal body that advises the British monarch
a meeting, and a ... is a toilet, the smallest room in a house

explanation.surface: A committee assembles in the tiniest room in the building.
explanation.walkthrough: The Privy Council is a formal body of advisers to the British monarch; 'privy' also means an outdoor toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Privy Council is the group of advisers to the British sovereign.

clue.text: Stupid person, possibly a fool

definitions.meaning: a fool is a creamy fruit dessert, one example of a sweet course

explanation.surface: Someone calls another an idiot, perhaps a jester.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'pudding' is the dessert course, and a fool is a dessert of fruit and cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Pudding is slang for a dull, stupid person and is also the dessert course.

clue.text: I make money investing little cash, getting right mark

indicators.note: to invest is to clothe or surround, so the money word wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: to mint is to make coins
p is a penny, a small amount of British cash

explanation.surface: A banker says that putting in a little money earned the right result.
explanation.definitionFit: An imprint is a mark pressed into a surface.

clue.text: Artist's image: a fool with love

parts.note: a pic is a picture or image
an ass is a fool
love is nil in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A painter's portrait shows a fool who is in love.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is read as 'has': the artist has PIC, then ASS and O.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo Picasso was a famous Spanish artist.

clue.text: Want to remove borders, so open

indicators.note: the edges of the want word are taken off, leaving its middle

parts.note: want means poverty, a lack of means

explanation.surface: A desire to tear down boundaries and be candid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Want' looks like a verb meaning desire; here it is the noun meaning need, POVERTY, which loses its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means done openly, not hidden.

clue.text: Elected (given office), hard being thorough

parts.note: a party that wins is in, voted into power
a dept, or department, is an office of government
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A newly elected official takes office and finds the work hard going.
explanation.definitionFit: An in-depth study is detailed and thorough.

clue.text: Compound speed of a berk?

parts.note: berk is British slang for a fool, as is nit
rate means speed

explanation.surface: Someone asks how fast a silly person goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'berk' is mild British slang for an idiot; 'nit' is another.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitrate is a chemical compound, a salt of nitric acid.

clue.text: Belief that plants have souls confusing simian male

indicators.note: confusing mixes up the letters of the word beside it

explanation.surface: A botanist's mystical idea baffles an ape-like man.
explanation.definitionFit: Animism is the belief that natural things, including plants, have spirits.

clue.text: Record years since the Wall Street Crash?

definitions.meaning: an old gramophone record played at ... revolutions per minute

definitions.text: years since the Wall Street Crash?
definitions.meaning: the Crash was in 1929, and this puzzle appeared in 2007, that many years later

explanation.surface: A historian keeps count of how long it has been since the markets fell.
explanation.definitionFit: A 78 is an old shellac gramophone record, named for its playing speed.
